verses.zh: 以色列众人聚集到希伯仑见大卫，说：「我们原是你的骨肉。
verses.en: All Israel joined David at Hebron and said, “Look, we are your very flesh and blood![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “look, your bone and your flesh [are] we.”

verses.zh: 从前扫罗作王的时候，率领以色列人出入的是你；耶和华―你的　神也曾应许你说：『你必牧养我的民以色列，作以色列的君。』」
verses.en: In the past, even when Saul was king, you were Israel’s commanding general.[NOTE:1] The Lord your God said to you, ‘You will shepherd my people Israel; you will rule over my people Israel.’”
notes: Heb “you were the one who led out and the one who brought in Israel.”

verses.zh: 于是以色列的长老都来到希伯仑见大卫王。大卫在希伯仑耶和华面前与他们立约，他们就膏大卫作以色列的王，是照耶和华藉撒母耳所说的话。
verses.en: When all the leaders[NOTE:1] of Israel came to the king at Hebron, David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord. They anointed David king over Israel, in keeping with the Lord’s message that came through Samuel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “elders.”
Heb “by the hand of Samuel.”

verses.zh: 大卫和以色列众人到了耶路撒冷，就是耶布斯；那时耶布斯人住在那里。
verses.en: David and the whole Israelite army[NOTE:1] advanced to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus).[NOTE:2] (The Jebusites, the land’s original inhabitants, lived there.)[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all Israel.”
Jebus was an older name for the city of Jerusalem (cf. Josh 15:8; Judg 1:21).map For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and there [were] the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land.”

verses.zh: 耶布斯人对大卫说：「你决不能进这地方。」然而大卫攻取锡安的保障，就是大卫的城。
verses.en: The residents of Jebus said to David, “You cannot invade this place!” But David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).

verses.zh: 大卫说：「谁先攻打耶布斯人，必作首领元帅。」洗鲁雅的儿子约押先上去，就作了元帅。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] David said, “Whoever attacks[NOTE:2] the Jebusites first will become commanding general!”[NOTE:3] So Joab son of Zeruiah attacked[NOTE:4] first and became commander.[NOTE:5]
notes: Verse 6 inserts into the narrative parenthetical information about Joab’s role in the conquest of the city. Verse 7 then picks up where v. 5 left off.
Or perhaps “strikes down.”
Heb “head and officer.”
Heb “went up.”
Heb “head.”

verses.zh: 大卫住在保障里，所以那保障叫作大卫城。
verses.en: David lived in the fortress; for this reason it is called the City of David.

verses.zh: 大卫又从米罗起，四围建筑城墙，其余的是约押修理。
verses.en: He built up the city around it, from the terrace to the surrounding walls;[NOTE:1] Joab restored the rest of the city.
notes: Heb “to that which surrounds.” On the referent here as “the surrounding walls,” see HALOT 740 s.v. סָבִיב.

verses.zh: 大卫日见强盛，因为万军之耶和华与他同在。
verses.en: David’s power steadily grew, for the Lord of Heaven’s Armies was with him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and David went, going and becoming great, and the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, Lord of hosts] was with him.”

verses.zh: 以下记录跟随大卫勇士的首领，就是奋勇帮助他得国、照着耶和华吩咐以色列人的话、与以色列人一同立他作王的。
verses.en: These were the leaders of David’s warriors who, together with all Israel, stood courageously with him in his kingdom by installing him as king, in keeping with the Lord’s message concerning Israel.

verses.zh: 大卫勇士的数目记在下面：哈革摩尼的儿子雅朔班，他是军长的统领，一时举枪杀了三百人。
verses.en: This is the list of David’s warriors:[NOTE:1] Jashobeam, a Hacmonite, was head of the officers.[NOTE:2] He killed 300 men with his spear in a single battle.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and these are the number of the warriors who were David’s.”
The marginal reading (Qere) has “officers;” the consonantal text (Kethib) has “the Thirty” (see v. 15).
Heb “he was wielding his spear against 300, [who were] slain at one time.”

verses.zh: 其次是亚合人朵多的儿子以利亚撒，他是三个勇士里的一个。
verses.en: Next in command[NOTE:1] was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was one of the three elite warriors.
notes: Heb “after him.”

verses.zh: 他从前与大卫在巴斯・达闵，非利士人聚集要打仗。那里有一块长满大麦的田，众民就在非利士人面前逃跑；
verses.en: He was with David in Pas Dammim[NOTE:1] when the Philistines assembled there for battle. In an area of the field that was full of barley, the army retreated before the Philistines,
notes: Some read here “Ephes Dammim.” See 1 Sam 17:1.

verses.zh: 这勇士便站在那田间击杀非利士人，救护了那田。耶和华使以色列人大获全胜。
verses.en: but then they made a stand in the middle of that area. They defended it[NOTE:1] and defeated the Philistines; the Lord gave them a great victory.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “delivered it.”
Heb “and the Lord delivered [with] a great deliverance.”

verses.zh: 三十个勇士中的三个人下到磐石那里，进了亚杜兰洞见大卫；非利士的军队在利乏音谷安营。
verses.en: Three of the thirty leaders went down to David at the rocky cliff at the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine force was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.zh: 那时大卫在山寨，非利士人的防营在伯利恒。
verses.en: David was in the stronghold at the time, while a Philistine garrison was in Bethlehem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

verses.zh: 大卫渴想，说：「甚愿有人将伯利恒城门旁井里的水打来给我喝！」
verses.en: David was thirsty and said, “How I wish someone would give me some water to drink[NOTE:1] from the cistern in Bethlehem near the city gate!”
notes: Heb “Who will give me water to drink?” On the rhetorical use of מִי (mi) here, see BDB 566 s.v. f.

verses.zh: 这三个勇士就闯过非利士人的营盘，从伯利恒城门旁的井里打水，拿来奉给大卫。他却不肯喝，将水奠在耶和华面前，
verses.en: So the three elite warriors[NOTE:1] broke through the Philistine forces and drew some water from the cistern in Bethlehem near the city gate. They carried it back to David, but David refused to drink it. He poured it out as a drink offering to the Lord
notes: Heb “the three,” referring to the three elite warriors mentioned in v. 12.

verses.zh: 说：「我的　神啊，这三个人冒死去打水，这水好像他们的血一般，我断不敢喝！」如此，大卫不肯喝。这是三个勇士所做的事。
verses.en: and said, “God forbid that I should do this![NOTE:1] Should I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?”[NOTE:2] Because they risked their lives to bring it to him, he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three elite warriors.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Far be it to me from my God from doing this.”
Heb “with their lives.” The same expression occurs later in this verse.
Heb “These things the three warriors did.”

verses.zh: 约押的兄弟亚比筛是这三个勇士的首领；他举枪杀了三百人，就在三个勇士里得了名。
verses.en: Abishai the brother of Joab was head of the three[NOTE:1] elite warriors. He killed 300 men with his spear[NOTE:2] and gained fame along with the three elite warriors.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Syriac reads “thirty” here and at the beginning of v. 21; this reading is followed by some English translations (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV, NLT).
Heb “he was wielding his spear against three hundred, [who were] slain.”
Heb “and to him [reading with the Qere] there was a name among the three.”

verses.zh: 他在这三个勇士里是最尊贵的，所以作他们的首领；只是不及前三个勇士。
verses.en: From[NOTE:1] the three he was given double honor and he became their officer, even though he was not one of them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “more than.”
Heb “of the three.”

verses.zh: 有甲薛勇士耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅行过大能的事：他杀了摩押人亚利伊勒的两个儿子，又在下雪的时候下坑里去杀了一个狮子，
verses.en: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave warrior from Kabzeel who performed great exploits. He struck down the two sons of Ariel of Moab;[NOTE:1] he also went down and killed a lion inside a cistern on a snowy day.
notes: Heb “the two of Ariel, Moab.” The precise meaning of אֲרִיאֵל (ʾariʾel) is uncertain; some read “warrior.” The present translation assumes that the word is a proper name and that בְּנֵי (bene, “sons of”) has accidentally dropped from the text by homoioarcton (note the preceding שְׁנֵי, shene).

verses.zh: 又杀了一个埃及人。埃及人身高五肘，手里拿着枪，枪杆粗如织布的机轴；比拿雅只拿着棍子下去，从埃及人手里夺过枪来，用那枪将他刺死。
verses.en: He even killed an Egyptian who was 7½ feet[NOTE:1] tall. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand as big as the crossbeam of a weaver’s loom; Benaiah attacked[NOTE:2] him with a club. He grabbed the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand and killed him with his own spear.
notes: Heb “5 cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches for the standard cubit, this individual would be 7.5 feet (2.3 m) tall.
Heb “went down to.”

verses.zh: 这是耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅所行的事，就在三个勇士里得了名。
verses.en: Such were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who gained fame along with the three elite warriors.

verses.zh: 他比那三十个勇士都尊贵，只是不及前三个勇士。大卫立他作护卫长。
verses.en: He received honor from[NOTE:1] the thirty warriors, though he was not one of the three elite warriors. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
notes: Or “more than.”

verses.zh: 军中的勇士有约押的兄弟亚撒黑，伯利恒人朵多的儿子伊勒哈难，
verses.en: The mighty warriors were:Asahel the brother of Joab,Elhanan son of Dodo, from Bethlehem,[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

verses.zh: 哈律人沙玛，比伦人希利斯，
verses.en: Shammoth the Harorite,[NOTE:1] Helez the Pelonite,[NOTE:2]
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:25 has the variant spelling of “Shammah.”
The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:26 has the variant spelling of “Paltite.”

verses.zh: 提哥亚人益吉的儿子以拉，亚拿突人亚比以谢，
verses.en: Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,Abiezer the Anathothite,

verses.zh: 户沙人西比该，亚合人以来，
verses.en: Sibbekai[NOTE:1] the Hushathite,Ilai[NOTE:2] the Ahohite,
notes: In 2 Sam 23:27 this individual’s name is given as “Mebunnai.”
The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:28 has the variant “Zalmon.”

verses.zh: 尼陀法人玛哈莱，尼陀法人巴拿的儿子希立，
verses.en: Maharai the Netophathite,Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,

verses.zh: 便雅悯族基比亚人利拜的儿子以太，比拉顿人比拿雅，
verses.en: Ithai[NOTE:1] son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjaminite territory,Benaiah the Pirathonite,
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:29 has the variant spelling “Ittai.”

verses.zh: 迦实溪人户莱，亚拉巴人亚比，
verses.en: Hurai[NOTE:1] from the valleys of Gaash,Abiel[NOTE:2] the Arbathite,
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:28 has the variant spelling “Hiddai.”
The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:31 has the variant spelling “Abi-Albon.”

verses.zh: 巴路米人押斯玛弗，沙本人以利雅哈巴，
verses.en: Azmaveth the Baharumite,[NOTE:1] Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:31 has the variant spelling “Barhumite.”

verses.zh: 基孙人哈深的众子，哈拉人沙基的儿子约拿单，
verses.en: the sons of Hashem[NOTE:1] the Gizonite,Jonathan son of Shageh[NOTE:2] the Hararite,
notes: In 2 Sam 23:32 this individual’s name is given as “Jashen.”
The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:33 has the variant spelling “Shammah.”

verses.zh: 哈拉人沙甲的儿子亚希暗，吾珥的儿子以利法勒，
verses.en: Ahiam son of Sakar[NOTE:1] the Hararite,Eliphal son of Ur,[NOTE:2]
notes: In 2 Sam 23:33 this individual’s name is given as “Sharar.”
The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:34 has the variant “Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite.”

verses.zh: 米基拉人希弗，比伦人亚希雅，
verses.en: Hepher the Mekerathite,Ahijah the Pelonite,

verses.zh: 迦密人希斯罗，伊斯拜的儿子拿莱，
verses.en: Hezro[NOTE:1] the Carmelite,Naarai son of Ezbai,
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:35 has the variant spelling “Hezrai.”

verses.zh: 拿单的兄弟约珥，哈基利的儿子弥伯哈，
verses.en: Joel the brother of Nathan,[NOTE:1] Mibhar son of Hagri,
notes: The parallel text of 2 Sam 23:36 has the variant “Igal son of Nathan from Zobah.”

verses.zh: 亚扪人洗勒，比录人拿哈莱〈拿哈莱是给洗鲁雅的儿子约押拿兵器的〉，
verses.en: Zelek the Ammonite,Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,

verses.zh: 以帖人以拉，以帖人迦立，
verses.en: Ira the Ithrite,Gareb the Ithrite,

verses.zh: 赫人乌利亚，亚莱的儿子撒拔，
verses.en: Uriah the Hittite,Zabad son of Achli,

verses.zh: 流便人示撒的儿子亚第拿〈他是流便支派中的一个族长，率领三十人〉，
verses.en: Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, leader of the Reubenites and the thirty warriors with him,

verses.zh: 玛迦的儿子哈难，弥特尼人约沙法，
verses.en: Hanan son of Maacah,Joshaphat the Mithnite,

verses.zh: 亚施他拉人乌西亚，亚罗珥人何坦的儿子沙玛、耶利，
verses.en: Uzzia the Ashterathite,Shama and Jeiel, the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

verses.zh: 提洗人申利的儿子耶叠和他的兄弟约哈，
verses.en: Jediael son of Shimri,and Joha his brother, the Tizite,

verses.zh: 玛哈未人以利业，伊利拿安的儿子耶利拜、约沙未雅，摩押人伊特玛、
verses.en: Eliel the Mahavite,and Jeribai and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam,and Ithmah the Moabite,

verses.zh: 以利业、俄备得，并米琐八人雅西业。
verses.en: Eliel,and Obed,and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter begins the account of David becoming king over "all Israel." This becomes a key
theme. God will restore "all Israel" (i.e., post-exilic and eschatological).

- The majority of this chapter deals with the exploits of David's mighty men of valor (i.e., his
private mercenary army, cf. 2 Samuel 23).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 11:1-3

1Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
2In times past, even when Saul was king, you were the one who led out and brought in Israel;
the Lord your God said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall
be prince over My people Israel.'" 3So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David
made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord; and they anointed David king
over Israel, according to the word of the Lord through Samuel.

11:1-9 This information comes from 2 Samuel 5:1-10.

11:1 This is also recorded in 2 Samuel 5. The "all Israel" is a key phrase. David had become king of Judah
but not Israel (i.e., the northern tribes). Saul's remaining son, Ish-bosheth, had been made king of Israel by Abner
(cf. 2 Samuel 2).

11:2 "you were the one who led out and brought in Israel" This is an idiom for military leadership.

▣ "shepherd" This VERB (BDB 944, KB 1258, Qal IMPERFECT
is used of YHWH. It was an ANE title of kingship.

The opening line of Ps. 23:1 is literally "YHWH is the one shepherding me." The only
VERBAL is the Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE (BDB 944, KB 1258). The concept
of YHWH as Shepherd was a royal title in the ANE (i.e., Hammurabi). In the OT it is used in the sense of

- a description ‒ Ps. 78:52; Ezek. 34:11-13

- a covenant title ‒ Ps. 80:1

- a metaphor ‒ Isa. 40:11; Jer. 31:10

- the Messiah as Shepherd ‒ John 10:11; 1 Peter 2:25

It is such powerful imagery because of

- the close and constant presence of the shepherd with the sheep

- the sheep's need of an ever-present caretaker and protector

▣ "prince" This NOUN (BDB 617) is a royal title used of the kings of Israel.

- Saul ‒ 1 Sam. 9:16; 10:1

- David ‒ 1 Sam. 13:14; 25:30; 2 Sam. 5:2; 6:21; 7:8; 1 Chr. 17:7; 2 Chr. 6:5

- Solomon ‒ 1 Chr. 29:22

- Messianic ‒ Isa. 55:4; Ezek. 34:24; 37:24-25

▣ "My people Israel" YHWH is the true Shepherd and King. These are His covenant people.

11:3 "elders" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER.

▣ "to the king at Hebron" TeThe Chronicler does not mention David being king over only part of Judah for
a period (cf 1 Chr. 3:4).

▣ "covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "anointed" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "ANOINTING" IN THE BIBLE.

▣ ""according to the word of the Lord through Samuel" This is literally
"by the hand of Samuel." "Hand" is used idiomatically. This refers specifically to 1 Samuel 16.

God spoke to His people in several ways.

- historic events

- visions, dreams

- theophanies

- Urim and Thummim

- prophets, cf. 1 Chr. 11:3,10

- written records of His revelation (i.e., the Bible)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (it's uniqueness and inspiration)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 11:4-9

4Then David and all Israel went to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants
of the land, were there. 5The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, "You shall not enter here."
Nevertheless David captured the stronghold of Zion (that is, the city of David). 6Now David had said,
"Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first shall be chief and commander." Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, so
he became chief. 7Then David dwelt in the stronghold; therefore it was called the city of David.
8He built the city all around, from the Millo even to the surrounding area; and Joab repaired the rest
of the city. 9David became greater and greater, for the Lord of hosts
was with him.

11:4 "Jebus" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM.

▣ "Jebusites" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE.

▣ "Zion" See Special Topic above.

Jerusalem was built on seven hills; one of them, on which David built his palace, was Zion. It became
a designation for the entire city. Here an editor added "(that is, the city of David)."

11:7 "the stronghold" There seems to be a distinction between

- the city of Jebus

- the stronghold within the city, which was captured many years after the city itself (cf. Jos. 15:63; Jdgs. 1:21; 2 Sam. 5:7)

11:8 "the Millo" This (BDB 571) may refer to the repair of the terraces by "filling in" the dirt (cf. 2 Sam.5:9;
1 Kgs. 9:15,24; 11:27; 2 Chr. 32:5). The Millo may have supported the foundations of David's palace on the hill called "Zion."

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"repaired"

TEV, NJB
"restored"

JPSOA
"rebuilt"

REB
"reconstructed"

This is the common term for "life" (BDB 310, KB 309, Piel IMPERFECT).
It usually refers to humans or animals. Only here it relates to the repair of fortifications of Jerusalem and in Neh. 4:2 to
the rebuilding of a protective outer wall of Jerusalem.

11:9 "David became greater and greater" This is a Hebrew idiom. "David continued to continue to
become powerful" (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT plus the Qal
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE CONJUNCTION of the same root, which denotes emphasis).
David's greatness expanded because YHWH was with him.

▣ "the Lord of hosts" David's greatness was because the
Lord of hosts was with him (cf. 1 Chr. 12:18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 11:10-11

10Now these are the heads of the mighty men whom David had, who gave him strong support in his kingdom,
with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the Lord concerning Israel.
11These constitute the list of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite,
the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred whom he killed at one time.

11:10-41 This information comes from 2 Sam. 23:8-39.

11:10 "these are the heads of the mighty men" These mercenary warriors of David are structured into

- the three, 1 Chr. 11:12,18,20,24,25,42; related to 1 Chr. 11:17-19

- the thirty, 1 Chr. 11:11,15,20,25,42

- the second rank of the three, 1 Chr. 11:21

They came from several tribes to reinforce the "all Israel" theme.

The exploits of these men are told by Josephus in Antiq. 7.3.1,2 and 7.12.4.

If it is the same person, the name and numbers are different from 2 Samuel.

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why does Chronicles leave out so much of the historical information found in Samuel?

- Why was the meeting at Hebron so theologically significant?

- 1 Chronicles 11:3 mentions "the word of the Lord"; to what revelation does this refer?

- Explain the relationship between Jebus and Zion.
